newsitem.title: THAILAND: Interbank steady, interfinance rates rise-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Interbank steady, interfinance rates rise-dealers.

text.p: Thai interbank rates held mostly steady on early Wednesday afternoon but short-term interfinance rates surged on tightened domestic liquidity stemming from heavy demand for U.S. dollars in the currency market, dealers said.

The overnight interbank offered rate was quoted at 12.00-13.00 percent at 0700 GMT against 13.00-13.50 percent in the morning as market jitters prompted a flight of funds from small finance firms to large companies, traders said.
The overnight interfinance rate rose to about 20 percent from 14 percent quoted late on Tuesday, a dealer said.
"They are not too high at the moment but I would expect interfinance rates to go higher later," a dealer at Thai Danu Bank said.

Jitters about Thailand's economic fundamentals, withdrawal of foreign investors from a prolonged bearish stock market, and concerns about economic policy uncertainty combined to depress market sentiment, dealers said.
"I think it is all these factors together including rumours of conflicts within the (government) economic dream team," a dealer said.
